results.question: how long do i keep tax records
results.answer:
**STEP 1**  


**STEP 2**  
You must retain tax records as long as they may be needed for the administration of any provision of the Internal Revenue Code. In practice, that means keeping records that support an item of income or deduction on a return until the period of limitations for that return expires (Table 3 lists those periods) [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16).  

If you have employees, you must keep all employment‑tax records for at least **four (4) years** after the date the tax becomes due or is paid, whichever is later [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16).



**Sources:**
1. [irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf (Page 16)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16)

results.question: why do i need to keep business records
results.answer:
**STEP 1.**  


**STEP 2.**  
You need to keep business records for several reasons:

- To **monitor the progress of your business**. Good records let you see whether your business is improving, which items are selling, and what changes you need to make. [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=11)  
- To **prepare accurate financial statements** such as income (profit and loss) statements and balance sheets. [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=11)  
- To **prepare your tax returns**. Records must support the income, expenses, and credits you report. [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=11)  
- To **support items reported on tax returns** and be ready for IRS inspection. You must keep your records available at all times for IRS review, and you may be asked to explain the items reported if an audit occurs. [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=11)



**Sources:**
1. [irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf (Page 11)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=11)

results.question: what accounting method should i use
results.answer:
**STEP 1.**  


**STEP 2.**  
If you need to keep track of inventory, you must generally use an **accrual method** for purchases and sales [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=5).  
Certain small‑business taxpayers may choose the **cash method** instead and can also treat inventoriable items as materials and supplies that are not incidental [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=5).



**Sources:**
1. [irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf (Page 5)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=5)

results.question: cash or accrual accounting whats the difference
results.answer:
**STEP 1**  


---

**STEP 2**  
The IRS explains the two main accounting methods as follows:

- **Cash method**: you record income in the tax year you actually receive the money, and you record or deduct expenses in the year you pay them [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=5).  
- **Accrual method**: you record income in the year it is earned, even if payment arrives later, and you record or deduct expenses in the year they are incurred, whether or not you pay them that year [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=5).



**Sources:**
1. [irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf (Page 5)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=5)

results.question: can i deduct business travel
results.answer:
**STEP 1.**  


**STEP 2.**  
Yes – you can deduct the ordinary and necessary expenses of traveling away from home for your business [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/317-irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf#page=40). If the trip is overnight or long enough that you need to stop for sleep or rest to properly perform your duties, you can also deduct the cost of meals and lodging [[2]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/317-irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf#page=41).



**Sources:**
1. [irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf (Page 40)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/317-irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf#page=40)
2. [irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf (Page 41)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/317-irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf#page=41)

results.question: what should i track for taxes and for travel expenses
results.answer:
**STEP 1 – Passages that answer the question**


---

**STEP 2 – Answer**

When preparing your business taxes, **track all deductible expenses** and record each one as it occurs; otherwise you may forget them when you file your return [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=11).  
Also **identify the source of every receipt** you receive so you can separate business‑from‑non‑business income and taxable‑from‑nontaxable income [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=11).

For travel‑related deductions, **record the ordinary and necessary expenses you incur when traveling away from home for your business**.  You qualify as traveling away from home only if the travel meets the IRS conditions that are listed in the guide [[2]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/317-irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf#page=40).



**Sources:**
1. [irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf (Page 11)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=11)
2. [irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf (Page 40)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/317-irs_publication_334_tax_guide_small_business.pdf#page=40)
